title: Quantization impact inspector and candidate thresholding playbook
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Summary: Build an automated, repeatable inspector and playbook that evaluates the semantic and task-level impact of low-bit quantization profiles (AWQ and GPTQ) across candidate model configurations (int8, int4, hybrid). This ticket consolidates datasets, evaluation harnesses, metric thresholds, and rollout gates so that model change/config changes (quant profiles, bitwidth toggles, kernel selections) are validated before serving and can be monitored continuously in production.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A reproducible eval pipeline (one-click CI job) that runs AWQ/GPTQ profiles for specified models and outputs a standardized report (metrics and deltas). 2) A candidate threshold table (per-model and per-route) that flags unacceptable regressions. 3) Dashboards and alerting hooks wired to production telemetry for ongoing drift detection. 4) Playbook documenting rollback, canary thresholds, and manual review steps. 5) A sample canary rollout executed with a non-critical customer route and telemetry validated.
experiment_plan: Overview: We'll run a factorial grid across models (small/medium/large variants of open LLMs), quant backends (AWQ, GPTQ), and bitwidths (int8, int4, hybrid layerwise). For each cell run: (a) deterministic eval set (30k prompts across cohorts: instructions, summarization, code, retrieval Q&A), (b) held-out user-style cohorts (from Canary buckets), (c) downstream task probes (SQuAD-like QA accuracy, code generation pass@1, summarization Rouge-L), and (d) semantic similarity probes (BERTScore, embedding cosine). Schedule: 2 weeks for initial grid at low-cost sampling; follow-ups adaptively increase cohort where delta > detection_threshold. Implementation notes: use evallib harness under /infra/evals, containerized runner with precise RNG seeds, and compare against a pinned fp16 baseline. Record per-example deltas and aggregate distributions. See artifacts for scripts and seed lists.
metrics_and_thresholds: Primary metrics: 1) Task accuracy delta (percentage points) — threshold: <= 1.5% drop vs baseline for high-sensitivity routes, <= 3% for low-sensitivity. 2) Semantic similarity (BERTScore F1) delta — threshold: <= 0.012 absolute drop. 3) Log-likelihood per-token delta — threshold: <= 0.18 nats. 4) Hallucination rate increase (precision of factual QA) — threshold: <= 2% absolute increase. 5) Latency and tail-latency: p95 increase <= 18% and absolute p95 <= route SLO. Additionally compute distributional KS-test p-value for embedding shifts; flag p < 0.001. All thresholds are configurable and scoped by route labels (high-sensitivity, medium, experimental).
rollout_strategy: 1) Local eval -> CI nightly runs -> Internal canary (5% traffic on non-critical routes) -> Gradual ramp (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated checks at each step. 2) If any primary metric exceeds threshold at a step, automatic rollback and an alert to SRE/ML-ops. 3) Provide manual override with required review checklist (PM + ML-Research signoff). Canary duration default: 48 hours per step. 4) For Dedicated/private customers support, use snapshot tests and customer-specific gating before any private deployment.
implementation_notes: Key engineering tasks: (A) Extend the eval harness to compute per-token LL deltas and sample-based KS stats; (B) Add AWQ/GPTQ runner adapters that produce canonical profile metadata; (C) Integrate with CI to publish artifact bundles and delta reports to object storage; (D) Add a lightweight compare endpoint that returns pass/fail per-route and recommended rollback reason codes; (E) Add a telemetry tag schema for quant-profile metadata in production logs. Performance trade-offs: some AWQ profiles reduce cost but show concentrated failure cases on long-context code generation; plan to add layerwise hybrid profiles. Operationally ensure results are reproducible by storing config+seed+model-hash with each run.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Small relative metric shifts may hide catastrophic edge-case failures (e.g., code compilation breaks). Mitigation: add focused edge-case probes (compilation smoke tests for code tasks, structured-output conformance tests). Risk: Canary traffic may unintentionally affect customer experience. Mitigation: run canaries on internal mirror routes and opt-in customers; keep canary traffic capped and include feature-flagged auto-rollback. Risk: Evaluation cost/time for full grid. Mitigation: multi-stage sampling with early stopping heuristics and cohort prioritization based on traffic distribution.
notifications_and_alerts: Set up Prometheus/Grafana alerts: - quant.regression.alert when any primary metric delta exceeds threshold for > 10 minutes; - quant.ks.alert when embedding KS p-value < 0.001 for > 5m; - quant.ll_tail.alert when p99 LL delta exceeds configured per-route limit. Hook alerts to #quant-regression slack channel and create incident template for automated pager duty escalation for P0 regressions.
qa_and_validation: QA steps: 1) Run the pipeline on a known-stable model change (sanity test) and assert zero flagged regressions. 2) Inject synthetic failure profiles (artificial noise in weights) to validate detection and rollout blocking. 3) Cross-validate semantic metrics with human review on random 200-example samples when a profile is flagged. 4) Run long-run stability job: nightly re-eval for 14 days to capture flaky regressions.
